key_insight: A patient-level multimodal MIL system that combines ultrasound images with clinical variables better distinguishes phyllodes tumors from fibroadenomas than image-only or clinical-only models.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help reduce unnecessary surgery for fibroadenomas while supporting timely excision of phyllodes tumors.
method: Each patient is modeled as a bag of breast ultrasound images using a foundation-model encoder plus attention-based multiple instance learning.
Clinical features (age, lesion size, echogenicity) are learned separately with gradient-boosted modeling.
Image and clinical outputs are fused with logistic score fusion to make the final patient-level prediction.
evidence_signal: In 5-fold patient-level cross-validation, logistic score fusion achieved AUC-ROC 0.780 and outperformed clinical-only GB, image-only MIL, and end-to-end multimodal MLP fusion.
watch_item: The findings are based on retrospective cross-validation, so external validation and workflow testing are still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Multimodal Multiple Instance Learning for Fibroepithelial Tumor Diagnosis in Breast Ultrasound
